vessels.name: The Kinzies' boat
vessels.rig_words: a Mackinaw boat of the trade

existence.note: Wau-Bun: on the morning of 15 August 1812 Mrs. Kinzie's boat 'had scarcely reached the mouth of the river' when the family were stopped and held there, and on the third day after the battle 'the family of Mr. Kinzie, with the clerks of the establishment, were put into a boat' for St. Joseph. That it is a Mackinaw boat, its size, timber and where it lies on the 14th, made ready below the house, are ours (L-vessels-3612).

vessels.doing: Made ready below the Kinzie house, laden: the family leaves by water in the morning.

dated.doing: Held at the river's mouth with the family aboard, as Wau-Bun tells it, while the column marches south along the beach.

vessels.name: The garrison's scow
vessels.rig_words: a flat-bottomed boat of the post

existence.note: Wau-Bun, of 6 April 1812: Ensign Ronan and five or six soldiers 'ascended the river in a scow, and took the mother, with her infant of scarcely a day old, upon her bed to the boat'. That the post's scow was a flat-bottomed bateau, its size and where it lies by the wharf are ours (L-vessels-3612).

dated.doing: Brought up the river to the Burns landing by Ensign Ronan's party, to carry Mrs. Burns and her baby down to the fort.
